terms.gloss: face, look towards (of places and peoples)
evidence: Caes. BG 1.1.6: Belgae spectant in septentriōnēs et orientem sōlem (Lewis & Short s.v. spectō)
Caes. BG 5.13: alter angulus ad orientem sōlem … spectat (Lewis & Short s.v. alter)

terms.gloss: of a place: lie towards, face, slope towards
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with ad or in + acc.
evidence: Caes. BG 1.1: Galliae pars ad septentriōnēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short calls this the classical sense of the word: a place, a building or a slope “inclines” towards a quarter. Lewis & Short, after Neue, gives no perfect or supine.

terms.gloss: face up to, confront (a danger); a different sense from facing a direction
evidence: Sall. J. 7.4: obviam īre perīculīs, to meet dangers courageously (Lewis & Short s.v. obviam)

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 312, 339.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
Lewis & Short: vergo
